claims.text: Laya uses a non-autoregressive model to answer choice, score and noul questions, with a router selecting checkpoints.

evidence.quote: **Multilingual, non-autoregressive System 1 decision engine.** Typed decisions over 100+ languages in a single forward pass — 33 ms — trained with reinforcement learning against strictly proper scoring rules (RLCD), with a router that picks the right checkpoint per request.

```python
from laya import Router

router = Router()  # downloads a checkpoint on first use; Router(preload=True) loads all three up front

state = "Hi, we were billed twice for March. Please refund the duplicate today or we will cancel our plan."
questions = {
    "department": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "Which department should handle this?",
                   "criteria": {"billing": "invoices, payments, refunds",
                                "technical": "bugs, outages, system errors",
                                "other": "everything else"}},
    "urgency": {"type": "score", "instructions": "How urgent is this?",
                "criteria": ["not urgent", "soon", "blocking"]},
    "churn_risk": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Does the user threaten to cancel or leave?"},
}

result = router.predict(state, questions)
print(result["answers"]["department"]["choice"])  # billing
print(result["answers"]["churn_risk"]["noul"])    # probability the answer is yes
print(result["routing"]["model"])                 # english

claims.text: Its self-hosted server exposes POST /v1/systemone for existing Jev clients; the underlying model is Laya rather than hosted Jev.

evidence.quote:
## Self-Hosting: HTTP Server (Jev-compatible)

`laya.serve` exposes the `Router` over HTTP on the same `POST /v1/systemone`
wire protocol as TypeSafe's hosted Jev API. Laya's answer payload is already
schema-identical to what Jev returns (`choice`/`score`/`noul` answers and a
`{input_tokens, output_tokens}` usage block), so an existing Jev client — e.g.
the [`hs-jev`](https://github.com/getmissionctrl/hs-jev) Haskell client — just
needs its `baseUrl` repointed; nothing else changes.

claims.text: Pass state and questions to Router.predict(), or use the HTTP server with device, checkpoint and optional authentication settings.

evidence.quote:
```python
from laya import Router

router = Router()  # downloads a checkpoint on first use; Router(preload=True) loads all three up front

state = "Hi, we were billed twice for March. Please refund the duplicate today or we will cancel our plan."
questions = {
    "department": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "Which department should handle this?",
                   "criteria": {"billing": "invoices, payments, refunds",
                                "technical": "bugs, outages, system errors",
                                "other": "everything else"}},
    "urgency": {"type": "score", "instructions": "How urgent is this?",
                "criteria": ["not urgent", "soon", "blocking"]},
    "churn_risk": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Does the user threaten to cancel or leave?"},
}

result = router.predict(state, questions)
print(result["answers"]["department"]["choice"])  # billing
print(result["answers"]["churn_risk"]["noul"])    # probability the answer is yes
print(result["routing"]["model"])                 # english

Configuration is by environment variable: `LAYA_HOST`, `LAYA_PORT`,
`LAYA_DEVICE`, `LAYA_PRELOAD`, `LAYA_MODELS` (comma list to preload),
`LAYA_THREADS` (cap torch intra-op threads for CPU inference — keep at or below
physical cores), `LAYA_AUTO_TASK`, `LAYA_MAX_LOADED` (checkpoints resident at
once, 2 by default; raise it to 3 when `LAYA_AUTO_TASK` makes a third one
reachable on demand, or the server rebuilds one every time routing switches),
and `LAYA_API_KEY` (when set, clients must
send `Authorization: Bearer <key>`). A client's `model` field is honoured when it
names a Laya checkpoint (`english`/`multilingual`/`typed-decisions`), otherwise
the router auto-selects by script/language.

claims.text: Confidence thresholds do not transfer directly from Jev, and options share a token budget. The authors emphasize task-specific specialization of base checkpoints.

evidence.quote:
Three things differ from Jev when you port a client:

* **Options per question.** A question's options share the checkpoint's option budget, `head_max_len` (192 tokens on `laya`, 256 on the other two), not Jev's cap of 255 options. In addition, the HTTP server (`laya.serve`) enforces an amplification guard of at most 100 choice options per question (`MAX_CHOICE_OPTIONS = 100`, rejected with 413 before inference). Once options overflow the token budget, around 20 options with a short description each, every option is trimmed to fit, so long or similar labels can reach the model reading the same ([Where Jev leads](#where-jev-leads)). Once they no longer fit the window at all, the library rejects the request with 422. For more candidates, narrow them first with `predict_shortlist` ([Honest limits](#honest-limits)).
* **Score levels.** Every level needs a description. A `null` level is rejected with 422 rather than scored and echoed back in `legend`.
* **`confidence`** on `choice` and `score` answers is 1 minus normalised entropy, a measure of how concentrated the distribution is, not Jev's `(n·p_max − 1)/(n − 1)`. A threshold carried over from Jev does not transfer. For one calibrated number on every question type, gate on `answer_confidence`, the probability of the reported answer.

* **The base checkpoints are near chance on typed-decisions zero-shot** -- 0.362 and 0.352
  against a 0.318 random baseline and a 0.461 majority-class baseline. The 0.766 figure comes
  from the checkpoint fine-tuned on that benchmark's own training split. Laya is a fast base to
  specialise, not a zero-shot decision engine.

sections.text: Truyền trạng thái và câu hỏi vào Router.predict(), hoặc cấu hình thiết bị, checkpoint và xác thực tùy chọn cho máy chủ HTTP.

sections.heading: Phạm vi và giới hạn
sections.text: Không thể chuyển nguyên ngưỡng tin cậy Jev; các lựa chọn dùng chung ngân sách token. Tác giả nhấn mạnh việc tinh chỉnh checkpoint nền theo nhiệm vụ.

tr.title: Laya: Jev uyumlu API sunan yerel karar motoru
tr.h1: Laya: Jev uyumlu API sunan yerel karar motoru
tr.description: Laya yerelde türü belirli kararlar üretir ve Jev uyumlu HTTP API sunar; güven değerleri ile seçenek sınırları farklıdır.
tr.summary: Otoregresif olmayan model choice, score ve noul sorularını yanıtlar; yönlendirici model kontrol noktasını seçer. Kendi sunucunuzda POST /v1/systemone üzerinden mevcut Jev istemcileri kullanılabilir; çalışan model Laya’dır.

sections.heading: Amaç ve hedef kitle
sections.text: Otoregresif olmayan model choice, score ve noul sorularını yanıtlar; yönlendirici model kontrol noktasını seçer.

sections.heading: Jev’in rolü
sections.text: Kendi sunucunuzda POST /v1/systemone üzerinden mevcut Jev istemcileri kullanılabilir; çalışan model Laya’dır.

sections.heading: Kullanım
sections.text: Durum ve sorular Router.predict() çağrısına verilir; HTTP sunucusunda cihaz, kontrol noktası ve isteğe bağlı kimlik doğrulama ayarlanır.

sections.heading: Kapsam ve sınırlar
sections.text: Jev güven eşikleri doğrudan taşınamaz; seçenekler token bütçesini paylaşır. Yazarlar temel modellerin göreve göre özelleştirilmesini vurgular.

it.title: Laya: motore locale di decisione con API compatibile Jev
it.h1: Laya: motore locale di decisione con API compatibile Jev
it.description: Laya produce decisioni tipizzate in locale e offre un'API HTTP compatibile Jev, con differenze nella confidenza e nei limiti delle opzioni.
it.summary: Un modello non autoregressivo risponde a domande choice, score e noul; un router seleziona il checkpoint. Il server autogestito espone POST /v1/systemone ai client Jev esistenti, ma esegue il modello Laya.

sections.heading: Scopo e destinatari
sections.text: Un modello non autoregressivo risponde a domande choice, score e noul; un router seleziona il checkpoint.

sections.heading: Ruolo di Jev
sections.text: Il server autogestito espone POST /v1/systemone ai client Jev esistenti, ma esegue il modello Laya.

sections.heading: Come si usa
sections.text: Si passano stato e domande a Router.predict(), oppure si configurano dispositivo, checkpoint e autenticazione facoltativa nel server HTTP.

sections.heading: Ambito e limiti
sections.text: Le soglie di confidenza Jev non si trasferiscono direttamente; le opzioni condividono un budget di token. Gli autori sottolineano la specializzazione dei checkpoint di base.
